definitions.explanation: Vegetables whose edible part grows underground, such as carrots, daikon radish, burdock root, and potatoes. A common category in Japanese cooking and nutrition.

examples.japanese: {根菜|こんさい}は{体|からだ}を{温|あたた}める。
{根菜|こんさい}たっぷりの{味噌汁|みそしる}を{作|つく}った。
examples.english: I made miso soup packed with root vegetables.

examples.japanese: {冬|ふゆ}は{根菜|こんさい}を{使|つか}った{煮物|にもの}がおいしい{季節|きせつ}だ。
examples.english: Winter is the season when simmered dishes made with root vegetables are delicious.

notes:
USAGE:
A culinary and nutritional term. Common root vegetables in Japanese cuisine include {大根|だいこん} (daikon radish), にんじん (carrot), ごぼう (burdock root), {里芋|さといも} (taro), and れんこん (lotus root). In traditional Japanese health beliefs, root vegetables are thought to warm the body, making them especially valued in winter cooking.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {根菜|こんさい}{類|るい}: root vegetables (as a category)
- {根菜|こんさい}の{煮物|にもの}: simmered root vegetables
- {根菜|こんさい}サラダ: root vegetable salad
- {根菜|こんさい}スープ: root vegetable soup
